holidays.name: National Cheeseburger Day
holidays.description: A day to honor America's favorite cheesy sandwich. Fans celebrate with a classic diner burger, a backyard grill-out, or a towering gourmet stack with every topping.
holidays.origin: The cheeseburger's origin is disputed. One popular story says Lionel Sternberger, a Pasadena, California cook, added a slice of cheese to a hamburger sometime between 1924 and 1926. The holiday itself is an unofficial modern observance.
holidays.funFact: In the best-known version of the story, a customer suggested the cheese. That makes the cheeseburger one of the few iconic foods that may have started as a diner's request.

holidays.name: Rice Krispies Treats Day
holidays.description: A day for the gooey, crunchy marshmallow squares that have been a lunchbox and bake-sale favorite for generations. Melt some butter and marshmallows, stir in the cereal, press it into a pan, and you're celebrating.
holidays.origin: Rice Krispies Treats were created in 1939 by Mildred Day and her team in the Kellogg's test kitchens. They were first made for a Campfire Girls fundraiser. The day is an unofficial observance created to honor the snack.
holidays.funFact: The treats were first made for the Campfire Girls to sell as a fundraiser. A no-bake dessert with three ingredients turned out to be a hit.

holidays.name: World Bamboo Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of bamboo, the towering grass that can become scaffolding, flooring, bicycles, paper, clothing, and dinner for pandas. Events promote bamboo as a sustainable resource.
holidays.origin: The World Bamboo Organization established the day in 2009. It was announced at the 8th World Bamboo Congress in Bangkok, Thailand, to raise awareness of bamboo's ecological and economic value.
holidays.funFact: Bamboo is technically a grass, and some giant species can grow around 3 feet in a single day. That makes it one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth.
